name: Mediterranean Chicken w/ Marinade

intro_html:
This is the kind of dinner that looks like a restaurant plate and costs like a quiet Tuesday. Boneless chicken breasts get a lemon, garlic, and oregano marinade, then bake over a bed of spinach with artichoke hearts, grape tomatoes, and black olives, finished with a shower of crumbled feta. One casserole dish, one oven, and the whole week of dinners walks out lined up in the fridge.

Here is where the math does the talking. Every serving lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein and just {{carbs}} grams of carbs. That is a full plate that keeps you satisfied without the mid-afternoon crash, and it clears our 40-gram protein floor with plenty of room to spare. Big Mediterranean flavor, small carb footprint, and no special skills required.

True shopping cost: about $69.33 across 14 servings, roughly $4.95 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $10.69 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $80.02. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html:
Here is the part that matters when the plan has to survive a real budget. This whole thing comes out to ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is a lemon-marinated, feta-topped Mediterranean dinner with {{protein}} grams of protein, for less than what a single fast-food combo costs you, times 14 nights you do not have to think about dinner.

Cheap does not have to mean sad, and expensive does not have to mean good. This plate proves both.
shop_smart: The cart for this one is friendlier than it looks. Chicken breast is the anchor, so buy the family pack and let the freezer hold the rest for next time. You want 5 1/2 pounds of boneless skinless breasts, and evenly sized pieces bake more predictably than a mix of thin and thick.

Lean on the canned aisle here, because it is doing real work. The artichoke hearts come as three 15 ounce cans, drained, and the black olives as three 14.5 ounce cans, drained. Canned is the honest buy for both, since fresh artichokes are a project and a price. Grab a 14 ounce bag of fresh spinach, six lemons for juicing, and the feta at 1 pound 6 ounces, crumbled. Whole olive oil, a head of garlic, and your dried oregano, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes round it out, and those last four are pantry staples you likely already own.
make_it: Start with the marinade, because it needs the most patience. In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, the juice from your lemons, the minced garlic, the oregano, salt, and black pepper.

Add the chicken to a large bowl or a sealable bag, pour the marinade over it, and toss or massage until every piece is coated. Seal it, refrigerate, and give it at least 4 hours, or overnight if you plan ahead. This is where the flavor gets in.
When it is time to cook, heat the oven to 400F.
Spread the spinach across the bottom of a casserole dish brushed with olive oil, and sprinkle the red pepper flakes over the top.
Lay the marinated chicken breasts on the spinach, then scatter the artichoke hearts, grape tomatoes, and black olives over and around the chicken. Pour any marinade left in the bag right on top.
Bake covered for 25 minutes, giving thicker breasts a few extra if they need it.

Pull it out, top each piece with the crumbled feta, and slide it back in uncovered for 5 more minutes to warm the cheese. Let the whole dish rest 5 minutes before you slice, so the juices settle instead of running out.
portion_html:
This recipe is built to make 14 servings, and the fair way to split it is to weigh, not eyeball. Set your empty container on the scale and zero it out, then weigh the full baked dish and divide that number by 14. That is your target weight per container. Portion each one to hit it, spooning a little of the chicken, the spinach, and the artichoke, tomato, olive, and feta medley into every box so no container gets shorted on the good stuff.

Weighing beats guessing every time. Guess and your first few boxes are heavy, your last few are sad, and the macros stop being true. Weigh and all 14 land at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, exactly as promised.

steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the marinade: olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken breasts to a large bowl or sealable bag with the marinade. Toss or massage to coat, seal, and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Spread the spinach across a casserole dish sprayed with cooking spray or olive oil, and sprinkle the red pepper flakes over the top.
Lay the marinated chicken on the spinach, then scatter the artichoke hearts, grape tomatoes, and black olives over and around the chicken, pouring any leftover marinade on top.
Bake covered for 25 minutes, adding a few minutes for thicker breasts.
Top each piece with crumbled feta, return uncovered for 5 minutes, then rest 5 minutes before slicing and portioning.
